review.notes:
Baseline text is v1 (DB1-EN040, 2004-10-12), an exact match to the goat cdb entry, annotated 'Basically pre errata'; v0 (MRL-073, 2002-09-16) predates it and is not recorded. Most of the script diff is effect renumbering (the GOAT file shifts e1-e7 to e2-e8); reading both files confirms the only behavioural deltas are the two summon-event clones, the Level-derived Tribute count, and EFFECT_FLAG_CANNOT_DISABLE being present on the modern attack-lock registrar but absent in the GOAT one, so a negating effect can switch off the historical card's cannot-attack lock. Conflicting evidence preserved: the modern printed text carries the Archfiend treatment that the modern script does not implement. Data anomaly: the packet's Retro Pack events list tcg-na 2024-08-23 next to tcg-eu 2008-07-08; the earliest_tcg_date used for dating (2008-07-08) is the sane one. No supported period snapshot falls after 2012-09-29, so no intermediate historical implementation is needed for v3-v5 and none is claimed.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Toon Summoned Skull). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: Modern printing adds 'always treated as an Archfiend card' (event c2, 2013); the record claims the pre-2013 card was not treated as an Archfiend, so Archfiend support/anti-support did not touch it. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_ac page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-16): "You can select a "Special Summon-only" Archfiend like "Fiend Skull Dragon" or "Toon Summoned Skull" with "Archfiend's Roar", but only if they were Summoned properly earlier in the Duel." Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings page (Internet Archive replay): "You can select a "Special Summon-only" Archfiend like "Fiend Skull Dragon" or "Toon Summoned Skull" with "Archfiend's Roar", but only if they were Summoned properly earlier in the Duel." The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [c1] d1 unresolved (inference only) at Edison, unresolved (inference only) at Tengu. [c2] d2 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. [c4] d3 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: the printed text gained the treatment line making the card always treated as an 'Archfiend' card, which switches on Archfiend support and anti-support that did not touch the pre-2013 card. Neither upstream script implements the name treatment - official/c91842653.lua and goat/c504700160.lua were read in full and both register only the Special Summon procedure, the Toon World destruction, the attack effects and the attack cost - so the historical implementation is correct for the earlier era by omission while the modern implementation is unfaithful on this point."
